programme.title: Wild Birds of Australia

programme.title: Great Parks of Africa
programme.desc: In the southern reaches of Africa's great Kalahari basin, everything is made tough. Ancient rivers harbour water deep underground, and these hidden lifelines forge a fragile link to survival. This is the Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park.

programme.title: City Wildlife Rescue

programme.title: How Britain Worked
programme.desc: Guy has a dual task: to get a Yorkshire saw mill - Gayle Mill in Wensleydale - up and running again, and then use it to make a replica of one of the less-celebrated inventions of the Victorian era: the first pedal-powered bicycle. Using his engineering skills, Guy helps the restoration team repair the ingenious turbine that's needed to power the whole mill, but which is currently leaking 43 litres of water a second.

programme.title: How Britain Worked
programme.desc: Guy visits Llandudno to help get this Queen of Victorian resorts up to scratch in time for the summer season. The great British seaside holiday was a largely Victorian invention.

programme.title: How Britain Worked
programme.desc: Guy's project here is the first piston engine ever built. The Newcomen Beam Engine was the first practical device to harness the power of steam and kick-started the Industrial Revolution by allowing coal mining to operate on an industrial scale.

programme.title: How Britain Worked
programme.desc: Guy helps the £500,000 restoration of the world's oldest surviving Brixham sailing trawler, the boat that launched the modern fishing industry and transformed the way a nation ate.
